profile.name: Dr. medic. Isabella Wilden
bio: Dr. Isabella Wilden has worked as a physician for more than 35 years. Her practice is dedicated entirely to bioidentical hormone therapy and orthomolecular medicine.

Licensed to practise medicine in four EU countries (Romania, Greece, Germany and Cyprus), she has cared for women from many cultures, backgrounds and stages of life. As a specialist in General Medicine and a certified Hormone Expert (Germany), she combines a broad medical view with deep expertise in women’s hormones. In 2023, she founded Hormonexperten to make this care available to women online, wherever they live.

mission.title: Helping women feel strong in their bodies again
mission.body: My mission is to help women take back control of their health and feel like themselves again. I listen closely. Having gone through these changes myself, I know how unsettling this new part of your life might feel. We work as a team: we look at your results, try, adjust and refine until your treatment truly fits you. And I stay by your side for as long as you need me.

story.title: From one woman to another
body: My path as a woman, a doctor, a mother and a partner has taken me through different countries, languages and stages of life. Changing countries more than once and adapting to new environments has made me a curious listener and compassionate doctor. New beginnings are part of who I am. They have shaped the way I see people and the changes in their lives.

My path as a doctor has been just as varied. General medicine, research and psycho-oncology are part of it, as are functional medicine, micronutrient therapy and acupuncture. Each of these fields gave me another way to understand people: their symptoms, but also their story and what truly moves them.
At 40, my own body began to change.

I gained weight, and within a short time, I needed glasses. Then came the diagnosis of Hashimoto’s. My hair grew weaker, and eczema appeared around my eyes. Food intolerances, digestive problems, tiredness and sleepless nights became part of those years. And then there were lumps in my breasts. It wasn’t one single change. It was so much, all at once.
All of this was now happening to me. My body. My sleep. My everyday life.

I was a doctor, and at the same time the woman living through these changes. My medical knowledge was with me, but experiencing it myself gave so much of it a different meaning. Premenopause, perimenopause, menopause and postmenopause became chapters of my own life. I also came to know hormone therapy through my own body.

While I was walking my own path through these stages, I cared for thousands of women, especially with hormonal concerns. Each one brought her own story: questions, hopes, worries and the wish to feel well again. I learned something from every one of them. Even after all these years, a single conversation can still widen my view and show me something I had never seen before.

Some of what my patients told me felt deeply familiar. Other stories showed me how differently each of us can experience this time. And so, over the years, my personal story and my medical experience have grown together.
This, for me, is what makes my work special: I bring my knowledge, the experience of caring for thousands of women, and my own experience as a woman.

body.heading: Behind every lab result: a woman with her own story.

body: When you tell me today that your body has changed and you no longer feel like yourself, I want to understand what that means for you. What you are missing. What weighs on you. And what you long to have back in your life.
Because behind every lab result is a woman with her own story. I want to make room for yours.

profile.name: Dr. Yvonne Tuszing, M.D.
bio: Dr. Yvonne Tuszing is a medical doctor focused on women’s hormonal and metabolic health. She brings hospital training from obstetrics and gynaecology together with ongoing research on metabolism in women.

Alongside her clinical work, she is a PhD candidate at European University Cyprus, researching metabolism and glucose metabolism in women with PCOS. Certified in bioidentical hormone therapy and peptide therapy, and licensed in Germany, Switzerland and Cyprus, she has been part of Hormonexperten since 2026 and today co-leads the online clinic.
At Hormonexperten, she brings together modern diagnostics, bioidentical hormone therapy and human metabolism in a clear path that enhances your life.

story.title: Your cycle, your fertility and your metabolism speak the same language. I treat them as one.
story.statement: My mission is to help women understand how closely their reproductive and metabolic health are connected, and to treat both together. I want women to make informed and long-lasting health decisions for a strong and healthy future.
body: I know this connection from my own life. From a very young age, I struggled with painful, heavy periods and PMS (pre-menstrual syndrome). Over the years, I lost more than 20 kilograms and made my metabolic health a priority. Along the way, my cycle and my reproductive symptoms improved, and eventually resolved. Every woman’s path is different, but my own body showed me what medicine is only beginning to write into its guidelines.

During my clinical training, I met many women with PCOS/PMOS, PMS, ovarian cysts or endometriosis who had surgery after surgery, without anyone looking at their hormonal and metabolic health. While surgery might be necessary in certain cases, it should not be the only option for women. Research simply moves faster than guidelines, and the link between hormones and metabolism is still being uncovered.

That link is exactly what I research in my PhD. In my consultations, I bring research and clinical practice together: a careful look at your hormones and your metabolism, cycle tracking if you wish, and support alongside or before fertility treatment.
story.closing: My role is to give you the knowledge to choose what is right for you.
